Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy
Re: Creative Group Facilitator, Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Team,
I recently came across your Creative Group Facilitator opening and wanted to introduce myself. I understand the position may have been filled, but I would welcome consideration for this or future opportunities with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

My background brings together adolescent behavioral health support, recovery group facilitation, visual arts education, and fitness and wellness programming. 

At Family Center for Recovery, I supported adolescents and adults in structured treatment settings. At Futures Recovery Healthcare, I facilitated recovery support groups and helped alumni connect with resources and coping strategies. More recently, as an art teacher, I have designed creative activities that encourage confidence, expression, and engagement.

I am especially drawn to opportunities to help young people strengthen self-esteem and positive self-talk through art, movement, drama-inspired expression, and mindfulness. My approach values practical DBT-informed skills and creative activities as complements to the work of licensed treatment professionals.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my experience might support your programming. I have attached my resume for your consideration. 

Thank you for your time.

Warm regards, Jennifer Winston

candidates.cover_letter:
Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

I am excited to apply for the Clinic Director position leading the launch of Adolescent Wellness Academy’s first North Carolina clinic. As a licensed clinical social work and case management leader with more than 15 years of experience across behavioral health, healthcare, higher education, and community services, I offer the clinical supervision, operational leadership, and change-management experience needed to build a strong program from the ground up. AWA’s opportunity to create a focused, family-centered PHP/IOP clinic for adolescents is especially compelling to me because it combines direct clinical impact with the chance to shape culture, quality, and sustainable growth from day one.

Throughout my career, I have led complex case coordination, crisis response, care transitions, quality assurance, policy development, talent development, budgeting, and resource allocation. I have also provided clinical supervision and operational management while partnering with healthcare providers, hospital leaders, community agencies, and other stakeholders. These experiences would enable me to recruit and develop clinicians, establish clear clinical and documentation standards, guide level-of-care decisions, and build trusted relationships with families and referral partners across North Carolina.

I would bring a practical, outcomes-focused approach to launch execution: hiring and onboarding a cohesive team; creating a supportive environment for early-career clinicians; establishing reliable crisis, documentation, and quality-review processes; and using assessment findings and utilization trends to strengthen care delivery. My Master of Social Work and ongoing Doctor of Social Work studies in leadership further support my ability to connect evidence-informed clinical practice with disciplined operations and organizational growth.

AWA’s values—Dare to Grow, Contribute to the Whole, Choose Kindness, Spread Optimism, and Deliver Results—reflect how I strive to lead: with accountability, collaboration, compassion, and a clear commitment to excellent outcomes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical and operational leadership can help AWA launch a high-quality adolescent program and establish a strong foundation for long-term success in North Carolina.
Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Ty Matthews, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I’m excited to apply for the remote Utilization Review Specialist – Behavioral Health position at Principles Recovery Center. My background combines hands-on behavioral health documentation and review support with outpatient addiction and mental health program leadership, giving me a strong foundation for the role’s authorization and medical-necessity workflows.

In my current role as Behavioral Health Documentation & Review Support at Kings Consulting and Analytics, LLC, I support documentation review for substance use disorder and mental health cases. I review intakes, diagnoses, treatment history, progress notes, service documentation, and supporting clinical records to identify gaps and help ensure records are complete, consistent, and ready for utilization review. I also synthesize clinical details in EHR/KIPU workflows to support authorization-related documentation, level-of-care alignment, and timely review decisions. Working alongside an experienced behavioral health consulting team has strengthened my review accuracy and understanding of utilization review processes.

Previously, as Program Director at Meta Addiction Treatment, I developed substantial experience in outpatient addiction and mental health services, program leadership, and case management. That work strengthened my ability to coordinate across teams, support treatment planning and continuity of care, maintain clear documentation, and keep client needs and program requirements in view.

I’m prepared to bring this experience to benefit and eligibility verification, prior authorization and pre-certification workflows, concurrent and continued-stay reviews, and medical-necessity support. My background includes supporting level-of-care alignment and authorization documentation; I’m ready to build on that foundation with the specific review standards and procedures used by Principles Recovery Center.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my documentation review experience and behavioral health program background can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Lindsey Duran

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Therapy position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. I believe my clinical experience, diverse background working with various populations, and dedication to providing compassionate, client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role, I provide therapeutic services to youth, adolescents, and adults with a wide range of mental health and behavioral health needs, including PTSD, depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, and substance use disorders. I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed care, to help clients navigate challenges, strengthen coping skills, regulate emotions, and work toward their individualized treatment goals. I strive to create a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment where clients feel heard, respected, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

In Community,

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Nicolette Gonyea

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. This opportunity is especially meaningful to me because it brings together my professional background in behavioral health and my own personal experience with the recovery process.

I am a former Registered Behavior Technician (RBT), with firsthand experience working in the behavioral health field. Through that experience, I developed an understanding of the importance of compassionate care, effective communication, confidentiality, and creating a supportive environment for individuals and families seeking services.

In addition to my professional experience, I have a personal connection to the substance use recovery field. I have personally gone through treatment and have maintained my sobriety for over 16 years. My own journey has given me a deep appreciation for how difficult it can be to reach out for help and how important it is to feel heard, respected, and supported without judgment. I understand how much that first conversation can matter, especially for someone who may be feeling uncertain or overwhelmed about seeking treatment.

After recently welcoming my third child, I am looking forward to returning to the workforce in a position where I can use both my professional experience and personal perspective to make a meaningful difference. I am particularly drawn to admissions because I would love the opportunity to be a reassuring first point of contact for individuals and families, helping them navigate the process and take the next step toward receiving care.

I am dependable, organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable communicating with people from different backgrounds and circumstances. I understand the importance of handling sensitive information appropriately, following through on responsibilities, and maintaining clear and professional communication. I am also eager to learn new systems and procedures and bring a positive, compassionate, and solutions-oriented approach to my work.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my background in behavioral services, my firsthand understanding of recovery, and my genuine passion for helping others to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team. I would love to be part of an organization that helps adolescents and families find the support and treatment they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, perspective, and dedication could make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely,

Nicolette Gonyea

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I'm happy to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I'm particularly excited about the opportunity to bring my remote admissions and enrollment experience into a role where I will also use the skills I've gained through peer support and crisis intervention.

My time as a Remote Admissions Advisor at Southern New Hampshire University gave me a strong grounding in the day-to-day work of guiding prospective students through the admissions process. I handled inbound and outbound phone calls and emails, provided information on academic programs and admissions requirements, collected and recorded prospective student information, maintained our CRM records, and routed inquiries to the appropriate admissions specialist. That experience helped me develop my skills in managing multiple remote interactions, communicating information effectively, maintaining accurate records, and assisting people in making decisions.

My professional experience has increasingly been in mental health, peer support, and crisis intervention. As a Peer Support Specialist with Experience Knows LLC, I provide individualized support via video call, utilizing active listening, empathy, and my own lived experience to help people work through their issues and find solutions. I've worked with Gaggle ReachOut, supporting K-12 students who were experiencing emotional distress. My volunteering with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, Crisis Text Line, National Runaway Safeline, and the NAMI Helpline has further developed my ability to have difficult conversations, respond to people in crisis with compassion, and to appropriately connect people with the right resources.

I think these experiences are absolutely complementary in a behavioral health and substance use admissions context. Getting into professional mental health or substance use treatment can be a very vulnerable thing for the individual and their family. The person answering that first call has the opportunity to genuinely make someone feel seen, heard, respected, hopeful, and empowered about what's to come (potentially for the first time in their life). I'd bring patience, professionalism, excellent communication skills, and a person-centered, experience-informed approach to every single interaction. All the while, of course, I'd adhere to the core values of timeliness, accurate documentation, and ensuring the caller understands their options and what comes next on their journey.

I'm also completing a formal Peer Support Specialist certification and am currently doing my BA in Consciousness, Human Potential and Positive Psychology at Maharishi International University. I've also done additional training in Youth Mental Health First Aid.

If given the chance, I'd be honored to bring my remote admissions experience, my crisis support background, and my commitment to compassionate care to your team. Many thanks for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

Naomi Ruth Jeeter

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in healthcare, patient care, administrative support, and customer service, I have developed strong communication, organization, and interpersonal skills that I believe would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Through my experience as a caregiver and healthcare professional, I have worked closely with individuals and families navigating challenging health situations, including patients with dementia, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s disease, diabetes, and other complex medical needs. These experiences have taught me the importance of empathy, patience, confidentiality, and clear communication, especially when supporting people during vulnerable moments.

In addition to my healthcare background, I have experience with administrative coordination, scheduling, customer relations, and managing day-to-day responsibilities. I am comfortable handling multiple priorities, communicating with different people, maintaining accurate information, and following through on tasks in a timely and organized manner. I am also familiar with Microsoft Office and Google Workspace and enjoy learning new systems and technologies.

What particularly attracts me to this opportunity is the chance to combine my healthcare experience with my administrative and communication skills while contributing to an organization that makes a meaningful difference in people’s lives. I understand that the admissions process is often the first step toward receiving help, and I would approach every interaction with compassion, professionalism, and a genuine commitment to helping individuals and families feel supported.

I am fluent in Portuguese and English, and understand some Spanish, highly adaptable, detail-oriented, and eager to contribute to a team focused on making quality mental health and recovery services more accessible.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and dedication to patient-centered care could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Julia Vila Nova

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in this position. I hold a degree in Health Education, am currently pursuing a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and have over three years of experience working as a substance use counselor. Throughout my career, I have worked with individuals from diverse backgrounds, providing support that considers each client’s unique needs, strengths, and challenges, in 1:1 and group counseling settings. 

In my current role, I manage a caseload of more than 50 clients while providing individualized counseling and education, coordinating care, facilitating group sessions, and maintaining accurate clinical documentation. I regularly incorporate cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) principles and realistic goal-setting into my work to help clients identify challenges, develop practical strategies, and make meaningful progress toward their goals. Managing multiple responsibilities has strengthened my organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to balance competing priorities while providing consistent, compassionate support.

One of the aspects of my work that I value most is building trusting relationships and creating an environment where individuals feel welcomed, heard, and supported. I believe that a safe, encouraging, and nonjudgmental environment helps people feel comfortable engaging with others, working through challenges, and building confidence in their abilities. I take pride in my strong client satisfaction ratings and in creating positive experiences through thoughtful communication, consistency, and reliable follow-through.


Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and commitment to supporting others align with your team’s needs.

Sincerely,

Jennifer Misko

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a professional background in behavioral health, care coordination, substance use counseling, and healthcare administration, I am confident in my ability to provide compassionate, organized, and effective support to individuals and families seeking treatment.

In my current role as a Care Coordinator and Substance Use Counselor at Intermountain Centers, I work closely with adolescents, families, healthcare providers, and community agencies to coordinate behavioral health services and ensure individuals receive appropriate levels of care. My responsibilities include conducting assessments, coordinating referrals, facilitating Child and Family Team (CFT) meetings, assisting families with treatment planning, and supporting individuals through complex behavioral health challenges. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate with individuals in distress, identify service needs, and guide families through the treatment process with empathy and professionalism.

I also bring experience working within Arizona’s behavioral health system, including coordinating services with Medicaid-funded programs, maintaining accurate clinical documentation, and collaborating with multidisciplinary treatment teams. I understand the importance of timely follow-up, confidentiality, HIPAA compliance, and clear communication when helping individuals access mental health and substance use treatment.

As a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking professional, I am able to support diverse populations and help reduce language barriers that may prevent individuals and families from accessing care. I hold a Master of Business Administration (MBA) and a Master of Healthcare Administration (MHA), and I am currently completing my Master’s degree in Addiction Psychology at Arizona State University. This combination of clinical knowledge and administrative education allows me to approach admissions coordination with both compassion and operational efficiency.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to serve as a supportive first point of contact for adolescents, adults, and families during challenging moments. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be overwhelming, and I believe every individual deserves to be met with patience, dignity, and reassurance.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, dedication, and commitment to accessible behavioral healthcare to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications align with the needs of your programs.

Leslie Bright

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Mooresville, NC

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker Associate (LCSWA) with a Master of Social Work degree and three years of experience supporting children, adolescents, and families, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to AWA's mission of providing compassionate, evidence-based mental health services to adolescents. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to join the founding clinical team and help establish a supportive, collaborative, and client-centered therapeutic environment.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong foundation in family-centered treatment, crisis intervention, case management, treatment planning, and trauma-informed care. In my current role as a Family Centered Treatment Specialist with Pinnacle Family Services, I provide individualized treatment and case management services to children and families in home and community settings. I develop treatment plans, facilitate interventions, collaborate with community partners, and support families in navigating challenges while promoting stability, resilience, and improved outcomes. This experience has strengthened my ability to build therapeutic relationships, identify individual and family needs, and implement interventions that support meaningful behavioral and emotional change.

Previously, as a Family Advocate at Pat's Place Child Advocacy Center, I supported children and families navigating difficult and often traumatic circumstances. I provided emotional support, crisis intervention, resource coordination, and advocacy while collaborating with multidisciplinary professionals to prioritize child safety and family well-being. My school social work experience at Hawthorne Academy further strengthened my ability to recognize and address the emotional, behavioral, academic, and social needs of at-risk students while developing interventions and connecting families with appropriate resources.

I believe my background in child and family services provides a valuable foundation for working with adolescents experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, behavioral challenges, and other mental health concerns. I am passionate about creating a therapeutic space where adolescents feel safe, understood, and empowered to develop healthy coping strategies and recognize their strengths. I also understand the importance of family involvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, individualized treatment planning, and consistent communication in supporting successful clinical outcomes.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, dedication to family-centered care, and passion for adolescent mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Being part of a new program would allow me to contribute not only to the care of adolescents and their families but also to the development of a positive clinical culture built on compassion, collaboration, and excellence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, experience, and commitment to serving children and families would make me a valuable addition to AWA's founding clinical team.

Sincerely,

Abigail Cornele, MSW, LCSWA

My name is Selena, and I am excited to be applying for the primary therapist position at North Carolina's first-ever AWA location! I am an LCSWA with multiple years of experience providing therapeutic support in numerous capacities, including as a behavioral health technician, case manager, and psychotherapist. I've also gained experience in a diverse range of therapeutic settings, such as an inpatient adolescent hospital, PHP/IOP mental health clinics, community health (including in-home), and outpatient therapy. The most influential experiences I've gained have been working in adolescent inpatient and PHP/IOP clinics, in which I became comfortable leading group therapy sessions, providing 1:1 individual therapy as well as family-based therapy, and working collaboratively with clinical teams consisting of numerous disciplines and treatment goals. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in the Operations Manager position with Adolescent Wellness Academy as you prepare to open your first North Carolina clinic. What excites me most about this opportunity is the chance to be part of something that can make a genuine difference in the lives of young people and their families. Throughout my career, I have found the most rewarding part of my work is knowing that what I do has a meaningful impact on someone else's life. That is something I experienced firsthand at Shine Support Services, and it is something I hope to continue in my next role.

At Shine Support Services, I helped build the Supportive Employment Program from the ground up. I operated and developed workflows, internal procedures, training materials, participant resources, and documentation standards to help establish the foundation for daily operations. More importantly, I had the opportunity to work directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, support their goals, and build relationships with their families and community partners. I loved being able to see the difference that consistent support and encouragement could make in someone's confidence, independence, and everyday life. I taught a coping skills class that incorporated Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) practices, giving participants the opportunity to learn and practice healthy coping strategies. Those experiences reminded me that meaningful progress is not always one big milestone. Sometimes it is the smaller moments of growth that make the work so worthwhile.

I also bring leadership and operational experience from Graphic Components, where I led the photopolymer department before being promoted to Project Manager. I coordinated departmental workflow, monitored quality, addressed production challenges, developed procedures and training documentation, and cross-trained employees and prospective hires. This experience strengthened my ability to organize competing priorities, support a team, solve problems, and create systems that help people do their jobs effectively.

My experience working with young people also extends to YPATC, a youth performing arts program in Florida, where my responsibilities ranged from scheduling appointments to teaching theater to children. I enjoyed being part of an environment where I could contribute both behind the scenes and directly to the experiences of young people. I have pursued the 40-hour Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) training coursework, further developing my understanding of behavioral support and different learning and support needs.

What draws me to AWA is the opportunity to bring these experiences together in a setting where the work has such an important purpose. I understand that a successful program depends on more than the services being offered. It also takes thoughtful organization, dependable staff, clear communication, consistent routines, and an environment where young people and their families feel supported. I would be excited to help build that foundation for AWA's North Carolina clinic.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, leadership, and passion for meaningful work could contribute to AWA's founding North Carolina team.

Sincerely,

Erica R. Warriner
